question: What is the shape of a standard intrauterine device?
explanation: Standard intrauterine devices are manufactured in a T-shape to fit the anatomical dimensions of the uterine cavity. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h1)

question: Why is an intrauterine device classified as a LARC method?

options.A: It causes permanent sterilization after single use
options.B: It provides long-acting and reversible protection
options.C: It needs replacement every single month
options.D: It requires daily oral administration by the client

explanation: LARC stands for long-acting reversible contraception, meaning it works for years at a time but fertility returns right after removal. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h1)

question: How do copper IUDs primarily prevent fertilization?

options.A: Blocking the fallopian tubes with scar tissue
options.B: Thickening the cervical mucus barrier completely
options.C: Suppressing the release of all female hormones

explanation: Copper ions trigger a local sterile inflammation in the uterus that damages sperm and stops them from reaching an egg. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h2)

question: A hormonal IUD prevents pregnancy mainly by doing what?

options.A: Thickening cervical mucus and thinning the womb lining
options.B: Releasing copper to poison mature ova directly
options.C: Increasing the motility of sperm inside the tubes
options.D: Stimulating immediate shedding of the uterine wall

explanation: Progestin released from hormonal IUDs thickens the cervical mucus and thins the womb lining, making it hard for sperm to pass or for a fertilized egg to attach. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h2)

question: Which copper IUD model is most commonly stocked in Nigerian public health clinics?
explanation: The Copper T 380A is the standard copper IUD distributed widely in Nigerian public health facilities because of its effectiveness and low cost. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h3)

question: A client requests an IUD that will make her monthly periods lighter. Which option is best?
explanation: Levonorgestrel-releasing IUDs thin the endometrium, which consistently leads to lighter and less painful menstrual bleeding. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h3)

question: Which of the following is an absolute contraindication for IUD insertion?
explanation: Inserting an intrauterine device during an ongoing pregnancy causes severe complications, making pregnancy an absolute contraindication. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h4)

question: What is the purpose of the bimanual examination prior to IUD placement?

options.A: To clear the cervical canal of any mucus plugs
options.B: To confirm the absence of systemic viral infections
options.C: To measure the exact hormone levels in the blood
options.D: To determine the size and position of the uterus

explanation: A bimanual examination allows the nurse or clinician to assess uterine orientation and size, preventing uterine perforation. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h4)

question: What instrument is used to measure the depth of the uterine cavity before IUD insertion?
explanation: A uterine sound is gently passed through the cervical os to measure the length and direction of the uterine cavity. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h5)

question: A nurse is removing an IUD from a client. What technique should be used?

options.A: Apply steady, gentle traction on the visible threads
options.B: Push the device deeper into the fundus before pulling
options.C: Twist the tenaculum firmly until the device drops out
options.D: Pull the threads rapidly with a sharp jerking motion

explanation: Steady and gentle traction on the threads allows the arms of the T-shaped device to fold and slide safely through the cervix. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h5)

question: When should a routine follow-up visit be scheduled after a new IUD insertion?

options.A: After one full year of use

explanation: Checking the client after her first menses helps confirm the IUD remains in place and rules out early expulsion. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h6)

question: What physical finding should a client report immediately when checking her IUD threads?

options.B: Feeling soft nylon strings near the cervix
options.C: Feeling the hard plastic stem of the device
options.D: Not feeling any threads inside the vagina

explanation: Feeling the hard plastic stem indicates that the IUD has partially or completely slipped out of the uterine cavity. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h6)

question: What is a primary risk if pregnancy occurs while an IUD is in place?
explanation: While IUDs prevent most pregnancies, any pregnancy that does happen with an IUD in place has a much higher chance of being ectopic. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h7)

question: A client presents with severe pelvic pain and fever weeks after IUD insertion. What is the priority nursing suspicion?
explanation: Fever and severe pelvic pain point toward an ascending uterine infection like pelvic inflammatory disease requiring urgent medical care. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h7)
